disclaimer: Indicative 2026 list API pricing (USD per 1M tokens) compiled for comparative budgeting. Always verify current vendor pricing pages before production commitments, or override rates directly in the interactive calculator.

models.name: GPT-5
models.best_for: General flagship reasoning, structured tool calling, and high-cache-hit agent loops
strengths: 90% cached input discount ($0.125/1M)
50% Batch API discount for async workloads
Strong output quality per dollar vs legacy frontier tiers
watchouts: Output tokens ($10/1M) are 8x input cost — verbose reasoning chains inflate spend
400k context window is smaller than 1M-context peers

models.name: GPT-4.1
models.best_for: 1M-token long-context coding diffs, strict JSON schema adherence, and deterministic instruction following
strengths: 1M token context window with low needle-in-a-haystack degradation
Lower output price ($8/1M) than GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4
50% Batch API discount + 75% prompt cache discount
watchouts: Base input ($2.00/1M) is 60% higher than GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro
Cache read discount (75%) trails 90%-discount competitors

models.name: o4-mini
models.best_for: STEM reasoning, automated code review, SQL synthesis, and cost-sensitive reasoning pipelines
strengths: Reasoning-model performance at $4.40/1M output
50% Batch API and 75% cached input discounts
Predictable budget for math/logic verification steps
watchouts: Hidden reasoning tokens count as billable output tokens
200k context window limits full-repo single-shot prompts

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4
models.best_for: Agentic software engineering, multi-file refactoring, and nuanced editorial writing
strengths: 90% prompt cache read savings ($0.30/1M) drastically cuts multi-turn agent cost
50% Message Batches API discount for offline evaluations
Top-tier agentic coding reliability with fewer retry loops
watchouts: Uncached input ($3/1M) and output ($15/1M) sit above GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro
Japanese CJK tokenization averages ~1.95x English character efficiency

models.name: Claude Opus 4
models.best_for: High-stakes architecture synthesis, security auditing, and complex executive research
strengths: Maximum reasoning depth where avoiding a single error justifies premium unit cost
90% cached input discount ($1.50/1M) and 50% Batch API support
Ideal as the 5%–10% escalation tier in a routed architecture
watchouts: $75/1M output makes unrouted high-volume chat prohibitively expensive
5x more expensive than Claude Sonnet 4 at list rates

models.name: Claude Haiku 3.5
models.best_for: Low-latency classification, Anthropic-stack guardrails, and high-cache customer support bots
strengths: 90% prompt caching brings repeated system-prompt reads down to $0.08/1M
Same Anthropic Messages API format as Sonnet 4 / Opus 4 for seamless tiering
50% Batch API discount ($0.40/$2.00 effective)
watchouts: Higher per-token list price than Gemini 2.5 Flash, DeepSeek V3, and Qwen3
Output ($4/1M) is ~6.7x higher than Qwen3 235B via OpenRouter

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.best_for: Full-codebase analysis, massive PDF/video ingestion, and Japanese/multilingual long-context RAG
strengths: 1M+ context window at $1.25/1M standard input (<=200k tier)
Efficient SentencePiece vocabulary keeps Japanese token inflation lower (~1.65x)
50% Batch API and 75% context caching support
watchouts: Prompts exceeding 200k tokens step up to higher long-context tier pricing on Google AI
75% cache discount trails 90% cache tiers on GPT-5 and Claude

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.best_for: High-throughput extraction, 1M-context document triage, and real-time SaaS copilot routing
strengths: 1M context window at $0.30/1M input — ideal for bulk PDF & transcript ingestion
Low Japanese token overhead (~1.65x) makes it a strong default for JP SaaS
50% Batch API discount reduces input to $0.15/1M
watchouts: Thinking/output tokens ($2.50/1M) can outpace ultra-cheap open-weight models if unconstrained
Complex multi-file code synthesis still benefits from Sonnet 4 / GPT-5 escalation

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.best_for: Cost-disruptive chain-of-thought reasoning, math/logic verification, and synthetic training generation
strengths: Reasoning performance at $0.55/$2.19 per 1M — roughly 4–5x cheaper than frontier closed models
Automatic prefix caching ($0.14/1M) + off-peak/batch savings
Open weights allow migrating to self-hosted RunPod GPUs at scale
watchouts: Long chain-of-thought traces multiply generated output tokens
Data residency compliance often requires US/EU OpenRouter or self-hosted endpoints

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.best_for: Bulk summarization, translation, synthetic labeling, and ultra-low-cost SaaS backends
strengths: Sub-$0.30 input and $1.10 output with automatic cache hits at $0.07/1M
Strong general coding and multilingual fluency for the price tier
Open weights eliminate single-vendor lock-in
watchouts: 128k context ceiling vs 400k–1M proprietary models
Enterprise privacy teams should route via zero-data-retention OpenRouter providers or self-host

models.name: Qwen3 235B (OpenRouter)
models.best_for: CJK/Japanese high-volume localization, cost-optimized RAG synthesis, and open-weight MoE pipelines
strengths: One of the lowest output prices ($0.60/1M) among large MoE models
Best-in-class CJK/Japanese tokenizer efficiency (~1.55x vs English)
Accessible via OpenRouter with zero-data-retention provider filtering
watchouts: No standardized 50% async Batch API across all serverless OpenRouter hosts
Prompt cache hit discounts vary by underlying inference provider

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick (OpenRouter)
models.best_for: English-heavy high-throughput pipelines, multimodal extraction, and portable self-hosted migration
strengths: Ultra-low $0.18/$0.60 per 1M open-weight MoE pricing on OpenRouter
1M-token context support with wide third-party GPU host competition
Smooth path from serverless API to dedicated RunPod vLLM cluster
watchouts: Higher Japanese token expansion (~2.10x) narrows its lead on CJK workloads
Serverless OpenRouter endpoints rarely offer native 50% batch queues
